messages:
deploy-bot: ALERT: canary v7.0.0 p95 latency +50% vs baseline on route 'completion-eu'. Autorevert scheduled in 4m. Telemetry: https://telemetry/redwood/v7.0.0
frida: Who's on operator? This started right at the start of the approved change window. Prefer human-check before auto revert.
nate: Oncall. Agree — change window, but this is big. Suggest suppress automatic revert, then decide: targeted pin vs full revert based on shard scope.
oliver: Quick triage: looks like EU shards 2/5 showing spikes, others steady. Maybe a node-level scheduling quirk with the new kernel tweak.
tam: If it's 2/5, let's do a targeted route pin for the EU slices and keep the rest of rollout intact. That keeps release velocity and minimizes customer impact.
frida: I can run the route-pin. Command: ```bash
rls route-pin --env canary --route completion-eu --to v6.9.7 --reason "p95 regression on subset of shards"
```
ops-bot: Autorevert will run in 240s. Operator override required to suppress.
frida: Taking operator. Suppress autorevert for 30m to give time for a controlled remediation and comms.
ops-bot: Operator override accepted. Autorevert suppressed for 30m.
ops-bot: Executing: rls route-pin --env canary --route completion-eu --to v6.9.7
ops-bot: SUCCESS: completion-eu route pinned to v6.9.7; traffic rebalanced.
nate: Monitoring metrics: p95 returns to baseline on pinned slices. Core rollout unaffected. Good.
legal-bot: Reminder: change-window public notice may be required if we widen rollback. Loop legal in if we prepare customer-facing email.
cs-bot: Drafting customer blurb: "We detected increased response times for a small subset of European inference traffic after a canary update. We routed that traffic to a prior version while we investigate. No data loss. Updates in 30 minutes."
frida: I'll post the short CS blurb and add the legal tag. Also creating follow-up ticket RL-9832 and attaching traces.
oliver: For RCA, initial traces point to increased KV cache churn when a new batching policy intersects short-sequence requests. Not sure yet if it's a runtime bug or config mismatch.
tam: Decision notes: manual intervention executed to prefer targeted pin over autorollback. Criteria used: shard scope (2/5), metric delta (>40% p95), and low error-rate (<1%).
frida: Adding a brief note to the release notes section: "v7.0.0: temporarily held on subset of EU traffic due to latency regression; investigation underway; no user data impacted." Will send to release-notes channel once legal okays.
nate: Leaving pin for 45m and watching for upstream regressions. If other shards degrade, we escalate to full revert.
ops-bot: Autorevert suppression will expire at +30m. Extend if needed via operator request.
frida: Thanks team  manual rollback decision and execution done, CS notified, legal looped, postmortem ticket created. Will follow up with RCA roadmap. :thumbsup:
